degree_note: Gonzaga awards the BA, BS and BFA (College of Arts and Sciences), BA, BS and BBA (School of Business Administration), BEd (School of Education), BA and BS (School of Engineering and Applied Science) and BSN and BS (School of Health Sciences); each degree is available in General and Honors versions. The university describes itself as offering 16 undergraduate degrees through 53 majors, 68 minors and 73 concentrations. Where the catalog index lists a major under two degrees (e.g., Biology (BA) and Biology (BS)) it is recorded once with 'BA or BS'. Concentrations are recorded as notes, not separate majors; the catalog's engineering degrees are styled BSCE, BSCpE, BSEE, BSEM, BSME, BSBE, BSCS, BSCY, BSDS but the index lists them as BS. School of Business Administration undergraduates earn the Business Administration BBA with concentrations (Business Analytics, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Finance, Human Resource Management, Individualized Program, International Business, Law and Public Policy, Management Information Systems, Operations and Supply Chain Management); only Accounting, Business Administration and Marketing are listed as separate BBA majors. Minors 66-69 below appear only in school-level catalog tables, not in the A-Z index. Excluded: graduate programs, graduate certificates, the JD, the Honors Program, Hogan Entrepreneurial Leadership Program (its minor is included), Military Science/ROTC, the Health Professions Pathways Program (pre-health advising), the 3+3 BA/BS-JD pathway, 4+1 master's pathways, and the MBA + BS in Engineering combined program.

Reed awards only the Bachelor of Arts (BA) for all majors. Reed states it offers 38 majors, 13 of them interdisciplinary; the public program list rendered 37 and the Dance-Theatre interdisciplinary major (listed on Reed's academics page and still described as active on its program page) is added as the 38th. Ad hoc (self-designed) interdisciplinary majors may be approved by petition but are not listed as a named program; they are included below with that note. Minors are offered only in the 17 fields listed; ad hoc minors are not available. Excluded: the 3-2 dual-degree programs in Engineering (Columbia, Caltech, RPI) and Forestry-Environmental Sciences (Duke), the Master of Arts in Liberal Studies, and the Pathway to Law School / Pathway to Premedical and Preveterinary Preparation advising programs, which the program page tags as 'Dual Degree/Special Program'. The list may be slightly incomplete because the source page loads additional entries dynamically.

UP awards the BA and BS (College of Arts & Sciences), BBA (Pamplin School of Business), BAEd and BSSE (School of Education), BSCE, BSCS, BSEE, BSEnvE and BSME (Donald P. Shiley School of Engineering) and BSN (School of Nursing & Health Innovations). Degree abbreviations are given as the Bulletin prints them; 'BA or BS' means the Bulletin lists both degrees for that major. The Bulletin's program list does not show concentrations, so none are recorded. Excluded from the majors list but shown in the Bulletin alongside them: the combined B.B.A./M.B.A. Program for Accounting Majors (dual degree) and the Post Baccalaureate Professional Computer Science Degree (Prof-B.C.S., a post-baccalaureate program). The Military Studies minor is offered through ROTC (Special Academic Programs). School attribution for minors is inferred from the Bulletin's URL paths.

Puget Sound awards the Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Science and Bachelor of Music; several majors (Chemistry, Economics, Psychology, Special Interdisciplinary Major) are offered as either BA or BS. The current Bulletin (bulletin.pugetsound.edu, Coursedog, 2026-27) renders its program list only via JavaScript and its PDF is on a robots-blocked Google Drive link, so it could not be read directly. The list was assembled from (1) the university's official 2026-27 Curriculum Guides and Checklists page (every major with degree), (2) the 2026-27 Academic Programs index (major/minor labels per department), and (3) the 'Undergraduate Degrees' section of the 2024-25 Bulletin PDF (pp. 18-19) for exact minor names; names were taken from the Bulletin where the sources differ, with the alternate name noted. Possibly incomplete or stale items are flagged in notes (Liberal Studies BA via FEPPS, Biophysics minor, Music minor naming, Latina/o Studies major). Tracks/concentrations/emphases within a major are noted, not listed separately; the Interdisciplinary Humanities Emphasis is an emphasis (not a major or minor) and is omitted. Excluded: Dual-Degree Engineering (3-2 with partner schools), pre-health advising tracks, the MAT, MEd Counseling, MPH, OTD/MSOT and DPT graduate programs.

Whitman awards only the Bachelor of Arts ('departmental majors lead to a Bachelor of Arts degree'). The catalog groups majors as Standard Majors (29), Combined Majors (34, including interdisciplinary programs such as BBMB and Brain, Behavior, and Cognition) and the Individually Planned Major; all are listed here as separate majors because the catalog lists them that way. Minors are called 'Minor Study Programs' (38). The catalog also lists four Concentrations (Global Studies, Human-Centered Design, Public Health, Social Justice) that can be added to any major; these are not majors or minors and are omitted. Combined/transfer programs omitted: 3-2 Engineering, Forestry & Environmental Management (Duke), and Oceanography (University of Washington); pre-law and pre-health advising omitted. Note: the catalog's 'At a Glance' page says 'seventy-one departmental majors', while the Overview of Academic Programs page enumerates 63 named majors plus the Individually Planned Major; the enumerated list is used here. The dynamic catalog.whitman.edu/programs index could not be loaded; the list comes from the catalog's static Overview of Academic Programs page.

Undergraduate degrees: Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Science (Willamette College, formerly the College of Arts & Sciences) and Bachelor of Fine Arts (Pacific Northwest College of Art). The catalog lists each degree variant as its own program entry (e.g. 'Biology (BA)' and 'Biology (BS)'); these are merged here as 'BA or BS'. Program entries that are emphases/tracks/concentrations of one major (Theatre's four emphases, English: Creative Writing Concentration, Chemistry: Biochemistry Track) are folded into the parent major with a note. Minor names are given exactly as the catalog titles them, including the ': WC' / ', WC' / ': PNCA' suffixes used to distinguish Willamette College and PNCA versions. Excluded: School of Law (JD, LLM, certificates), Atkinson MBA and other graduate programs, undergraduate certificates (CERT.*), the non-degree English Language and American Studies program, and accelerated/dual programs (Bachelor's + JD, + MBA, + MS Data Science) and the 3-2 Engineering and Forestry (Duke) partner programs. The dynamic program index did not render, so the list was built from the catalog sitemap's 147 program URLs; the sitemap appeared complete for programs but could theoretically omit a program not yet indexed.

Gettysburg awards the Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Science, Bachelor of Music (Performance) and Bachelor of Music Education; all majors are BA unless listed otherwise. The college's course catalog is in Workday (not web-readable), so the list is taken from the official All Programs index and each program page's 'Majors & Minors' table, which give program name, type and degree. Where the college lists a BA and a BS under the same name they are merged as 'BA or BS'; where it uses a distinct name (Environmental Science BS, Mathematical Economics BS, Art History and Museum Studies, English with a Writing Concentration, East Asian Studies Major - China/Japan) the distinct names are kept. Tracks within a major are noted, not listed separately. Excluded: Engineering Dual Degree (3-2 with Columbia, RPI, WashU, Pitt), Teacher Certification (7-12 Secondary) certification, Health Professions Advising, Pre-law Advising, ROTC, and the graduate programs (American History MA, Educational Design and Inquiry). The All Programs index labels Psychology 'Major, Minor', but the Psychology page's table shows only the Neuroscience minor, so no Psychology minor is listed.

Kalamazoo College confers only the Bachelor of Arts (B.A.); the catalog's degree-requirements page does not restate the degree type, so 'BA' is applied to every major. The online catalog (kzoo.edu/catalog) links the 2025-26 Academic Catalog PDF while its program pages show update dates of June-August 2026, so the list reflects the live 2025-26/2026-27 catalog as of Oct 2026. Kalamazoo offers 'concentrations' (interdisciplinary programs of ~6 courses, like a minor) alongside minors; the 12 concentrations are recorded in the minors list with note 'concentration'. Catalog names are used (e.g., 'Greek and Roman Cultures', 'Art - Studio Art', 'Business', 'Quantitative Economics'); the college's public academics page groups some of these under department names ('Classics', 'Art and Art History', 'Economics and Business', 'Chemistry and Biochemistry'). The catalog's 'Special Programs' section (Dual Degree Engineering, Complex Systems Studies, Interdisciplinary Courses, Language Courses, Physical Education, Shared Passage Seminars) and the Arabic course offerings are not majors or minors and are excluded; the Engineering Dual Degree is a 3-2 partner program.

Kenyon awards only the Bachelor of Arts (B.A.). The live course catalog is labeled 2026-27 (its breadcrumbs still read 2025-26). Kenyon offers both minors and 'concentrations' (interdisciplinary programs of 20+ semester hours); the 12 concentrations are recorded in the minors list with note 'concentration'. Catalog program names are used: the catalog lists one 'Classics' major with four tracks (Greek and Latin, Greek, Latin, Classical Civilization), one 'Modern Languages and Literatures' major (Tracks I-III, in Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Russian or Spanish) with minors in each of the eight languages, one 'Mathematics' major with three emphases, and one 'Environmental Studies' major with an Environmental Science track; the public departments-programs web page instead lists each language, Greek, Latin and Classical Civilization as separate majors and 'Mathematics and Statistics' as the major name. 'Asian and Middle East Studies' is a joint major (must be combined with a participating disciplinary major). The self-designed 'Synoptic Major' is listed as a major. Pre-health/pre-law advising and the engineering dual-degree partnerships are excluded.

Occidental awards only the Bachelor of Arts (B.A.); every major is a B.A. The self-designed 'Independent Pattern of Study' (48+ units, faculty committee, 3.25 GPA, approval by end of sophomore year) is listed as a major. Concentrations/emphases within a major (e.g., Biology: Molecular and Cell Biology, Environmental Science, Marine Biology; Art and Art History: Art History, Studio Art; Computer Science focus areas; CSLC foci) are recorded as notes, not separate majors. Catalog names are used where they differ from the Areas of Study web page: the catalog names the language minors 'French', 'Spanish', 'German' and 'Russian' (the web page calls them French Studies, Spanish Studies, German Studies, Russian Studies) and uses 'and' rather than '&'. Pre-law and pre-health advising, the 3-2 Engineering Program, the Core Program, College Writing Program and Athletics and Physical Activities offerings, and the M.A. in Biology are excluded.

Rhodes awards the Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) and Bachelor of Science (B.S.); a Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Studies is awarded only through the Liberal Arts in Prison program and is excluded. The catalog's 'Requirements for a Degree' page names the B.S. majors (Biology, Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Biomathematics, Chemistry, Computer Science, Environmental Science(s), Mathematics, Neuroscience, Physics); all other majors are recorded as B.A. by inference from that page, since most department pages do not state the degree. Interdisciplinary majors from the catalog's Interdisciplinary Study section are listed as separate majors (as the catalog does); the Self-Designed Interdisciplinary Major is included as self-designed. Concentrations and tracks within a major (e.g., Art History: Museum Studies; Chemistry: ACS-certified and Drug Design track) are notes, not separate majors. The Political Science major and minor are housed in the Department of Politics and Law. Certificates (Journalism, Geographic Information Science, Music Industry Studies, Pre-Engineering, Undergraduate Certificate in Liberal Arts), the Search humanities sequence, ROTC, study-abroad programs, the Master of Science in Accounting and the Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Health & Society are excluded. The public majors-minors web page differs slightly from the catalog (it lists a combined 'Art and Art History', 'Modern Languages and Literatures' and 'Environmental Studies & Sciences' and omits the Business, Chemistry, Computer Science and Data Analytics minors); the catalog is followed.

Sarah Lawrence awards a single undergraduate degree, the Bachelor of Arts (registered with NYSED as 'Liberal Arts', HEGIS 4901). Students do NOT declare majors or minors; the list below is the college's roster of disciplines (areas of study), grouped into four broad areas (Creative & Performing Arts; History & the Social Sciences; Humanities; Natural Sciences & Mathematics), plus 14 'Cross-Discipline Paths' that are suggested interdisciplinary themes rather than programs. Students must take at least 10 credits in three of the four areas and may take no more than 50 credits in a single discipline. There are no minors. Science Third (a double-science seminar program), pre-health advising, and combined/dual degree programs are mentioned on the site but are not disciplines and are not listed here.

Skidmore awards the B.A. and the B.S.; the degree for each major is taken from the NYSED-registered Degree Programs table in the catalog (B.S. is used for Art (Studio), Business, Dance, Education Studies, Health and Human Physiological Sciences, Social Work, and Theater; all others are B.A.; the Self-Determined Major may be B.A. or B.S.). The catalog lists seven interdepartmental majors (Business-French, etc.) as separate registered programs, so they appear as separate majors here; Business-Political Science is flagged in the catalog as approved for phase-out and no longer accepting applications. The catalog's Degree Programs table also lists two Engineering Dual Degree (3-2) programs with Dartmouth College and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (B.S.), which are partner programs and are excluded here. Concentrations/tracks within majors are not listed. The www.skidmore.edu/academics/majors-minors.php page could not be fetched (robots.txt), so the catalog was used instead.

St. Olaf awards the Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) and the Bachelor of Music (B.M.); a B.A./B.M. double degree is possible. St. Olaf has no 'minors': its interdisciplinary 'concentrations' (approved programs of at least four courses) are the functional equivalent and are recorded in the minors list with note 'concentration'. 'Areas of emphasis' (three or more related courses within or beyond a major, e.g. finance within economics, ACS within chemistry, voice within B.M. performance) are recorded as notes on the relevant major, not as separate programs. Teaching-certification tracks (English, mathematics, biology/chemistry/physics, social studies) and the TEFL certificate option within the educational studies concentration are omitted. The 'Individual Major' is a self-designed major proposed through the Center for Integrative Studies. Pre-professional advising (pre-med, pre-law, engineering 3-2 etc.) is not listed.

Union awards the B.A. and the B.S. (degree shown per program in the catalog list; a few entries carry no degree label and are marked ''). The catalog lists, as separate program entries, both a department's standard major and its '(ID)' version; an ID (interdepartmental) major is formed by pairing two departments' ID programs into one major, so each '(ID)' entry below is one half of such a pairing and is noted 'interdepartmental (ID) major' - filter on that note if you want only standalone majors (47 standalone, 34 ID). The catalog also lists tracks as separate entries (Chemistry A.C.S. vs Chemistry Basic; three Visual Arts concentrations; Managerial Economics, which appears twice in the catalog and is listed once here); these are kept as the catalog lists them. 'Organizing Theme B.S./B.A.' is Union's self-designed major. Engineering majors (Biomedical, Civil, Computer, Electrical, Environmental, Mechanical) are B.S.; Civil and Environmental began Fall 2023 and are not yet ABET-accredited. Excluded as combined/partner programs: the 3+3 Accelerated Law Program and the Leadership in Medicine/Healthcare Management B.S. (joint program with Albany Medical College/Clarkson). The catalog's 'Majors, Minors, and Other Programs' page lists 'Mental Health Care' and 'Musical Theater and Vocal Performance' without a label; union.edu identifies both as minors (2025), so they are placed in minors. The 'Interdepartmental' and 'Interdisciplinary Studies' catalog headings contain only courses. Individual program pages could not all be opened (catalog rate-limited), so degree labels rely on the list page text.

Clark awards the B.A. and B.S.; degree designations below are as shown on the official majors-and-minors page. Interactive Media tracks are kept as a note on that major. In addition to majors and minors Clark offers 15 interdisciplinary 'concentrations' (Africana Studies; Arabic Studies; Business Data Analytics; Comparative Race and Ethnic Studies; Computational Science; Environmental Humanities; Ethics and Public Policy; Genocide and Human Rights; Geospatial Data Analytics; German Studies; Jewish Studies; Latin American and Latinx Studies; Law and Society; Peace and Conflict Studies; Urban Studies), which are not minors and are not listed below. A Dual Degree 3/2 Engineering Program, graduate degrees and graduate certificates are also listed on the source page and are excluded.

The College of Liberal Arts awards the B.A. and B.S. The Programs of Study page tags only some majors with '(BS)'; the catalog shows additional BS programs (Accounting BS, Finance BS, Cybersecurity BS, Biology BS, Chemistry BS ACS Traditional) alongside BA versions, so degree values below combine both sources and majors not confirmed as BS are recorded as BA, the default CLA degree. English has emphases (e.g., Creative Writing Emphasis) listed in the catalog as variants of the English major, not separate majors. Drew also offers a self-designed 'Special Major' (catalog quick link), 16 dual-degree/combined-degree pathways (Accounting, Data Science, Engineering, Environmental Management, Finance, Forestry, Law, Master of Divinity, Medical Humanities Health and Society, Medicine, Nutrition/Dietetics, Public Health, Religion, Software Engineering, Teaching, Theology & Ministry), 17 pre-professional advising programs, graduate/theological degrees and non-degree certificates, all of which are excluded here. Minor names on the site that carried a '(BS)' tag (because the card is shared with the BS major) are listed without the tag.

SPU awards the B.A. and B.S. (Nursing is a B.S.); degree designations are as printed in the catalog. The catalog's majors list prints each concentration/track as its own line item (e.g., 'Business Administration: Finance (BA)', 'Psychology: Animal Behavior Track (BS)'), and that format is preserved below; collapsing on the text before the colon gives 33 distinct major titles. The catalog also lists four teacher-certification 'Certificates' (Elementary Certification; P-12 Visual Art Certification; P-3 Early Childhood Certification; Secondary Certification) and two 'Other Programs' (AI and Society; Pre-Professional Health Sciences), which are excluded. A Student-Designed major is offered as BA or BS. Note: the 2026-27 list reflects SPU's recent program eliminations; several fields (e.g., Chemistry, History, Mathematics, Philosophy, Physics) now appear only as minors.

Lynchburg awards the B.A., B.S. and B.S.N. (Nursing), but the Majors and Minors page does not print a degree designation for each program, so 'degree' is left blank except Nursing; the catalog should be consulted for BA vs BS. Names are given as the page states them, with the words 'Major'/'Minor' included. Items marked 'nav only' appear in the site's Academics navigation menu but not in the program-finder cards, so the list may slightly over- or under-count current offerings. Excluded: the Engineering Dual Degree Program (3-2 partner program), two degree-completion programs (Abridged Bachelor of Educational Studies; Abridged Bachelor of Public Health), graduate pathways and pre-professional advising tracks.

Stetson awards the B.A. and B.S. (College of Arts and Sciences), B.B.A. (School of Business Administration), and B.M. and B.M.E. (School of Music); the School of Music also offers a B.A. in Music. The catalog itself lists several concentration-level programs as separate entries and that is preserved here: World Languages and Cultures (6 concentrations), Applied Mathematics (4), Physics (3: Physics, Applied Physics, Biophysics), Bachelor of Music in Performance (5 instrument areas) and Bachelor of Music Education (2). Collapsing those to their parent program gives roughly 58 distinct majors. Minors carry no degree designation; superscript footnotes in the CAS list mark minors administered by the School of Business Administration or School of Music, and the Business Administration minor is open only to Arts & Sciences and Music students. Excluded: a B.S. in Engineering available only through cooperative (3-2 style) programs with other universities, pre-professional advising programs, graduate and law programs.

Seattle University awards the BA, BS, BABA (BA in Business Administration, Albers School), BFA, BM, BSW and BS in Nursing. The list below comes from the university's official All Programs directory filtered to undergraduate (92 entries) rather than the catalog's A-Z pages, which did not render for the fetcher; the directory and the 2026-27 catalog are maintained by the same registrar and the catalog nav lists Cornish College of the Arts as a Seattle U college, so the Cornish BFA/BA programs (Acting & Original Works, Animation, Dance, Design, Film & Media, Game Art, Illustration, Interaction (UX) Design, Interdisciplinary Arts, Music BM, Musical Theater, Performance Production, Photography, Theatre BFA) are included as Seattle U undergraduate majors. The directory lists some subjects as separate entries by degree (e.g. 'Biology, BA' and 'Biology, BS'; 'Design, BA' and 'Design, BFA'); these are kept as listed. Minors appear two ways in the directory: as stand-alone 'X, Minor' entries and as a 'Minor' tag on a major's entry; both are included and the latter are noted. Specializations/tracks within majors are not shown in the directory and are not listed. Excluded: post-baccalaureate and undergraduate certificates (Diagnostic Ultrasound Post-Baccalaureate Certificate; GIS & Geospatial Technology Certificate; Post-Baccalaureate Pre-Professional Health Studies Certificate), accelerated bachelor's/master's programs and Law 3+3, which the catalog lists under 'Accelerated Programs and Law 3+3'.

Loyola awards the BA, BS, BBA, BAS (Bachelor of Applied Science), BCJ (Bachelor of Criminology & Justice, online), BDes (Bachelor of Design), BFA, BM, BME (Bachelor of Music Education), BMT (Bachelor of Music Therapy) and BSN. The bulletin lists each degree-plus-subject as its own program (e.g. separate BA and BS in Public Health, eight separate BM programs, three BMT programs), and those are kept as listed; concentrations and sequences within a program (e.g. Mass Communication sequences, Biological Sciences concentrations, Teacher Education tracks, University Honors curricula) are recorded as notes. Minors are listed by department in the bulletin; the Cross-College Programs page lists interdisciplinary minors (it says eleven exist but names eight). Excluded: Associate of Arts in Psychology and Associate of Science in Business (City College), Alternative Music Teacher Certification (certification-only), post-baccalaureate certificates, Pre-Nursing and Exploratory Studies (non-degree), dual-degree options with Universidad Loyola Andalucia (BBA Management, BBA Marketing, BA Mass Communication-Advertising), Physics Pre-Engineering dual degree, and the College of Law. The loyno.edu 'majors-and-minors' marketing page could not be fetched. A BA in French appeared in the 2025-26 bulletin as 'being discontinued' and is not in the 2026-27 bulletin.

Pacific awards the BA and BS for most Forest Grove undergraduate majors (the official program list does not state which majors carry BA vs BS, so 'degree' is left blank unless the list names it), plus the Bachelor of Music Education (BME), Bachelor of Music Therapy (BMT), Bachelor of Social Work (BSW), Bachelor of Science in Dental Hygiene (BSDH, Hillsboro degree-completion program) and a hybrid Bachelor of Education (BEd) teacher-licensure program, which is listed on the all-programs page but not on the Forest Grove majors list and is not included below. The list comes from the university's official Forest Grove Undergraduate Programs page because the 2026-27 acalog catalog program listing could not be read; it may differ slightly from the catalog's program names. Items labeled 'Concentration/Emphasis' on that page (Accounting, Finance, International Business, Management, Marketing, Sports Marketing within Business Administration; Global Scholars) are recorded as notes, not as majors. 'Accelerated' labels (Chemistry, Computer Science, Sustainability and Adaptation) indicate 3-year accelerated options. Excluded: Pacific Pathways pre-professional tracks (pre-med, pre-law, pre-PT, pre-pharmacy, etc.), 3:2 dual-degree pathways (Engineering Science 3:2, Kinesiology & Athletic Training 3:2, Natural Sciences/Engineering), Pharmacy 3+3, post-baccalaureate certificates, and all graduate/professional programs.

Goucher confers a single undergraduate degree, the Bachelor of Arts (the college's curriculum pages refer only to 'Bachelor of Arts Degree Requirements', 120 credits), so every major below is a BA; the programs page itself does not print degree abbreviations. The list comes from goucher.edu's official Undergraduate Programs page and program pages because the acalog catalog listing could not be fetched; names follow those pages. The page lists 'Environmental Studies: Environment & Society' and 'Environmental Studies: Environmental Science' as separate entries although each is a concentration of the Environmental Studies major/minor; both are kept as listed. Arts Management is a concentration (27 credits) taken alongside an arts major, not a major or minor, and is not listed. Concentrations within majors (e.g. secondary education, dance science) are noted, not listed separately. Excluded: Premed/Prehealth Studies (pre-professional advising), the Columbia University 3+2 engineering dual degree, B.A./B.S. nursing dual degrees with Notre Dame of Maryland and Villanova, 4+1 B.A./M.A. programs, Johns Hopkins and Loyola Maryland partnership programs, and the post-baccalaureate premed program.

Ohio Northern's undergraduate colleges (Getty College of Arts & Sciences, Dicke College of Business Administration, T.J. Smull College of Engineering, Raabe College of Pharmacy's undergraduate programs) award the BA, BS, BFA, BM, BSBA, BSN and BS in engineering disciplines, but the Majors & Minors page does not state the degree for any program, so 'degree' is left blank throughout. The page tags each entry as Major, Minor, Concentration, Pathway, Preprofessional Program and/or Graduate Program; only Major and Minor tags are used here. Entries tagged only 'Concentration' (Actuarial Science, Advanced Energy, Advanced Mathematical Studies, Aerospace Engineering, Applied Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Automotive Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Brain and Behavior, Clinical and Counseling Psychology, Cybersecurity, Environmental Engineering, General Psychology, Honors Program, Manufacturing, Manufacturing Management, Mathematics with Teacher Licensure, Music Individualized Studies, Music Performance, Music Sound Recording Technology, Robotics, Sustainable Engineering) are concentrations within majors and are not listed; the page does not say which major each belongs to. Excluded: Pharmacy (Pharm.D., tagged Graduate Program), LAW - JD, 'Law - Pre-Law/3+3' (pre-professional/3+3 program tagged Major and Minor on the page), Pre-Medicine and other Pre- preprofessional programs, Engineering Exploratory Pathway, ROTC - Air Force Pathway, and the 'Undecided' placeholder.

Saint Mary's awards the BA and BS only (Nursing is a BS, not BSN). The college's 'Majors & Minors' page lists each degree variant and each concentration as a separate line (e.g. 'Anthropology, Archaeology Concentration, BA'; 'Communication: Media Studies, BA'); here each discipline is one major with degree variants and concentrations/tracks folded into the note. Only page 1 (A-E) of the 3-page official list could be loaded (query-string pages are blocked to crawlers), so programs F-Z were compiled from the official department pages and the 2025-26 catalog PDF; names for those may differ slightly from the official list (e.g. the catalog calls the Spanish major 'Spanish and Latin American Studies, BA' and lists Accounting as 'Public Accounting, BS' / 'Corporate Accounting, BA'). Excluded: certificates (Biliteracy, Computer Science, Digital Photography, Ethics, Media Production, Practical Political Leadership, Professional Writing), the Dual Degree (3-2) Engineering partner program, pre-professional advising (pre-med, pre-law, etc.), and teaching-credential pathways (Single Subject 4+1, Math BA/SSTE). The Performing Arts BA is the LEAP online degree-completion program for professional dancers. Minors are called 'Minor'. The catalog says minors are available in nearly all major disciplines; list is believed complete but is possibly missing a minor from a department page not fetched.

La Verne awards the BA and BS, plus one named undergraduate degree, the Bachelor of Law and Public Service (BLPS). The catalog states each program's degree in its title (e.g. 'Chemistry (BA/BS)'); minors are titled '<Subject> Minor'. Business Administration has six concentrations (Business Finance, Business Management, Human Resource Management, Information Technology, International Business, Marketing), folded into that major's note; the catalog also lists a 'Concentration in Teaching, Single Subject' (a credential-preparation option, not a major). Several majors appear twice in the A-Z index because they are offered both in the traditional program and in the Accelerated Program for Adults/regional campuses; each is listed once here. Excluded: the Associate of Arts in General Studies, undergraduate certificates, teaching-credential and 4+1 pathways (the Integrated Teacher Preparation Program is noted on Elementary Education), pre-law/pre-health advising, and all graduate programs. The catalog's own Interdisciplinary Programs section includes the self-designed 'Create Your Own Major'.

Hamline awards the BA, BS, BBA and BFA. The Program Finder labels each entry as Undergraduate Major / Minor / Online Bachelor's / Pre-professional / Certificate and gives the degree. Where a major is also offered as an online bachelor's degree-completion version (Business Administration, Psychology) it is listed once here with a note; Organizational Leadership and the Education Major for Paraprofessionals are online-only majors. The self-designed 'Flexible Curriculum' is offered as both major and minor. Excluded: pre-professional programs (Pre-Engineering, Pre-Health, Pre-Law, Pre-Medicine), the undergraduate Music Production certificate, licensure-only programs, and all graduate/continuing-education programs. Caveat: this list comes from the university's Program Finder rather than the Bulletin itself; the Bulletin's department pages may list additional departmental minors not surfaced in the Program Finder, so the minors list is possibly incomplete.

Capital awards the BA, BS, BM (Bachelor of Music), BSN and BSW; the official Majors and Minors page states the degree only for Conservatory of Music programs and Nursing, so 'degree' is left blank for other majors. The page itself lists each education licensure area (e.g. Primary Childhood Education PK-5) and each religion ministry track as a separate major, and lists Music as separate BA and BM degrees by area; those are kept as listed. The page advertises '64 majors, 57 minors' but itemizes fewer. Excluded: Pre-Law, Pre-Law 3+3 Accelerated Program (with Capital Law School), Pre-Seminary, pre-health specializations (Pre-Athletic Training, Pre-Physical Therapy, Pre-Medicine, etc.), the Dual Degree (3-2) Engineering partner program, the Accelerated BSN second-degree option (same BSN major), the 'Interdisciplinary Studies' and 'ROTC & Military Science' headings (no majors itemized under them), and graduate, law and seminary programs. Minors are titled '<Subject> Minor' on the page.

Undergraduate and Graduate Catalog 2025-26 (no 2026-27 catalog was published online at time of collection; the plu.edu/academics/majors-minors page is blocked to automated fetching, so the catalog's 'Program/Curriculum Information' index was used). PLU awards B.A., B.A.C. (Communication), B.A.E. (Education), B.A.K. (Kinesiology), B.B.A., B.F.A., B.M., B.M.A., B.M.E., B.S., B.S.K., B.S.N., and B.S.W. The catalog lists majors with their degree(s); where one subject is listed twice with different degrees (Kinesiology B.A.K./B.S.K., Theatre B.A./B.F.A.) the catalog lists them as separate lines and they are kept separate here. Concentrations exist within Chemistry, Communication, Kinesiology (B.S.K.), Music (B.M., B.M.E.), Studio Arts (B.F.A.) and Theatre (B.F.A.) and are noted on the major, not listed separately. 2026-2027 University Catalog. Since the 2024 merger with Woodbury University the catalog covers four undergraduate-granting units: the College of Arts and Sciences (Redlands campus, incl. the Johnston Center), the College of Architecture, Design, & Media (Los Angeles campus), the School of Business & Society (incl. the Woodbury Business Institute and the evening 'BS Business' degree-completion program) and the School of Education. Every undergraduate major/minor record in the catalog is listed here with its school in the note so the reader can filter to CAS. Degrees awarded: B.A., B.S., B.B.A., B.F.A., B.M., B.Arch., B.Des. Program names are given exactly as the catalog titles them (e.g. 'Johnston, B.A.' is the Johnston Center self-designed degree; the five 'Music Performance: <instrument>, B.M.' programs are separate catalog records and are kept separate). Where a subject has both a B.A. and a B.S. record they appear as separate entries, as in the catalog. 'Global Business, B.S.' has two catalog records (BS.GBUS under School of Business & Society; BS.GLBS under a Global Business department) and is listed once. Caveat: the catalog sitemap was truncated by the fetch tool after code 'MS.INTD', so minor codes alphabetically after that point were found by probing (Philosophy, Physics, Political Science, Psychology, Public Policy, Religious Studies, Race and Ethnic Studies, Sociology and Anthropology, Spanish, Theatre Arts, Women/Gender/Sexuality Studies were confirmed); a minor with an unusual code could be missing. Excluded: credential/certificate programs, graduate degrees, and accelerated pathways (MBA, MPPA, DPT, PharmD, Engineering combined degree, pre-law/pre-health) that the redlands.edu site lists as 'pathways'.
